Reproduced the bug with a **fresh** build of the original source, then verified the fix on a fresh binary. Git history preserves both states: `a07b361` (bug) → `303fd18` (fix).

**Before fix (fresh build):**
```
$ ./helios --help      → advertises "version   Print the helios version"
$ ./helios version     → Unknown command: version    (exit=1)
```

**Stale-artifact trap confirmed:** after editing the source but *before* rebuilding, `./helios version` still printed `Unknown command` — the gitignored binary at the repo root was running old code. `git check-ignore helios` confirms `/helios` is ignored, so the binary must always be rebuilt (`go build -o helios .`) before verifying.

**After fix (fresh `go build -o helios .`), full matrix:**

| Command | Output | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| `--help` / `help` / `-h` | usage text | 0 |
| `--version` | `helios version 0.1.0` | 0 |
| `version` | `helios version 0.1.0` *(identical — shared helper)* | 0 |
| `ping` | `pong` | 0 |
| `bogus` | `Unknown command: bogus` + usage | 1 |
| *(no args)* | usage text | 0 |

Edge cases covered: no-args (help, exit 0), unknown command (usage + exit 1), and byte-exact agreement between `--version` and `version` output. `gofmt -l` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -v ./...` → `PASS` (6/6 table subtests, `ok helios 0.002s`).
